name: Frank Zappa
hook: A composer who mixed doo-wop, rock and modern classical music into satire, and whose son played guitar on Weird Al's Zappa pastiche.
blurb: Frank Zappa was born in Baltimore in 1940. As a teenager he loved R&B, doo-wop and the strange, noisy modern classical music of Edgard Varèse, and he spent his career mixing them with rock and jokes. He formed the Mothers of Invention in 1965, and their 'Freak Out!' (Verve, 1966) was the second rock double album. He said the Mothers' purpose was satire of everything. He broke the band up in 1969 for money reasons and kept recording huge amounts of music until he died in Los Angeles in 1993. He also campaigned prominently against censorship. His son Dweezil, a guitarist, plays on Yankovic's 'Genius in France'.
